```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

The package ships the scripts that reproduce every table, figure and number of
the accompanying article. They download the public data, so they are not run
when the vignette is built.

```{r}
Sys.setenv(BP_DATA = "data", BP_OUT = "article-output", BP_CORES = "4",
           OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS = "1")
source(system.file("article", "run_all.R", package = "beatpool"))
```

## What each step does

1. `01_data.R` calls `download_physionet()` for the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia
   Database, the MIT-BIH Supraventricular Arrhythmia Database and the
   St Petersburg INCART database, and `read_database()` to segment the first
   signal (lead II in INCART) into windows of 61, 31 and 43 samples around the
   annotated R peaks. It also downloads the 49 industry portfolios of the
   French data library and standardizes them within each year.
2. `02_heldout.R` leaves out one record at a time, or one patient in INCART,
   and estimates every operator from the others: `pool_spectral()`,
   `pool_covariance()`, `pool_bases()`, `hierarchical_pool()`,
   `energy_moment()` with `pool_shared()`, and `dct_basis()`. It records the
   mean per-beat error, the ratio of traces, the rate of `rate_distortion()`
   and the separation of normal and ventricular beats.
3. `03_summary.R` computes paired bootstrap intervals over records or patients
   and writes the tables and `values.tex`.
4. `04_figures.R` draws the figures.

The scripts live in `system.file("article", package = "beatpool")`.
